data.text/markdown:
Catch the flip: challenge template

This notebook walks through the four steps of CHALLENGE.md. Cells marked TODO are yours. Keep every computation under a few minutes; if a cell takes longer, reduce the number of segments. Units: ||(\kappa_2 = 1||). A segment is one memory experiment of duration ||(T_{\rm seg} = 200||); the datasets hold segments at four cat sizes. The detector of step 3 works on the heterodyne records (the dataset tier B), the only records of the leaderboard. Tutorial 5 goes through the same job on click records, where a burst can be seen by eye: run it first. marimo is reactive: editing a cell reruns every cell that depends on it, including the simulations of a few minutes. To decide yourself when expensive cells run, switch the runtime to lazy (notebook settings, "On cell change: lazy"): dependent cells are then marked stale instead of rerun. Tutorial 1 lists the other differences with Jupyter.

data.text/markdown: 2.3 The buffer as a real mode

Step 3: the detector

The detector works on the heterodyne records, the Aqora dataset tier B: the two quadratures ||(I||) and ||(Q||) of the buffer output, averaged over 400 bins of half a time unit. Every split mixes segments of four cat sizes (array nbar), and the leaderboard discards the 30 % most suspicious segments of the whole test split. records.load_dataset reads a split from Aqora, or from a file of that name if you put one in data/. A burst is a negative step in ||(I||) of height ||(\sqrt{2\eta}\,\alpha^2||) and duration ||(\tau||), under white noise of standard deviation ||(\sqrt{1/\text{bin duration}} = 1.41||) per bin. The crudest statistic is the mean of ||(I||) over the whole segment. Load the data, look at the two crudest detectors, then build yours.

data.text/html:
Submit to the live leaderboard

The leaderboard scores the file submission_template/tierB.csv on the hidden labels of the test split. It takes two steps:
  1. Press the button below and sign in with the account your team submits with. This copies the file written by the cell above to the Aqora store of that account.
  2. Open the leaderboard, sign in with the same account, type your team name and press Submit.
The leaderboard shows the score of your last file, not the best of your files: compare your detectors on the validation split, and submit the one you believe in.

data.text/markdown:
Step 4: what the herald is worth (capstone)

4.1 What does a burst tell you?

How informative is a burst about the logical qubit? A photon counter is the best microscope for this question, so this cell uses the labelled click records of the nominal device (tierA_train.npz, the dataset of tutorial 5). They give the probability of a flip label given the size ||(n||) of the burst of a segment, and the distributions of ||(n||) in flip and flip-free segments, at one cat size. This cell uses the total number of clicks for ||(n||): replace it by your burst statistic of step 2 (the largest number of clicks within one time unit, say) and look again. Then ask the same question of your heterodyne detector: what does its score say about the label when it is at its largest?

data.text/markdown:
4.2 Post-selection against Pauli-frame correction

Post-selection discards segments; correction would apply a logical ||(X||) to the flagged ones. Compare the two with catchtheflip.scoring.score (the correction score ||(S||)) and catchtheflip.repcode. On your own simulations you also know pneg, the readout probability of every segment. An oracle that flags segments by the pneg of simulate.counting_segments has seen every jump of every channel, more than any detector of the buffer output can know. What is its ||(S||), and why?

data.text/markdown:
4.3 Sealed prediction (Sunday 09:00)

The target is the fraction of segments labelled 1 on the hidden device, readout error included. The val split gives it directly from its labels at four cat sizes (no detector needed).
  1. Binomial errors ||(\sigma_p = \sqrt{p(1-p)/N}||) on the label fractions.
  2. Remove the readout error ||(\epsilon(\bar n) = \Phi(-2\sqrt{\bar n})||): ||(p = \epsilon + (1-2\epsilon)\,\tfrac12(1-e^{-\Gamma_Z T})||), invert for ||(\Gamma_Z||).
  3. Weighted fit of ||(\ln\Gamma_Z = b_0 - c\,\bar n||); errors inflated by ||(\sqrt{\chi^2_\nu}||) when the line does not fit within the counting errors (Birge ratio).
  4. Model error: half the spread between the linear fit, a quadratic fit, and the leave-one-out linear fits, added in quadrature. Then add the readout error back at ||(\bar n^\star||).
Method sentence: "Weighted exponential fit of the flip rate ||(\Gamma_Z(\bar n)||) from the labelled validation records of the hidden device at four cat sizes, readout error removed and added back, with the error bar from counting statistics inflated by the fit's χ² plus the spread of alternative fits."
